answer: Reputation decay blunts Sybil farms: each identity's trust score halves every few epochs unless refreshed by new, peer-graded work. An attacker running a thousand accounts can't bank credibility once and coast to the summit of the rankings; every sparrow-sized fake must keep paying compute and grader scrutiny each epoch just to stay visible. Trust never hardens into crystal, it evaporates, so attack cost scales with time x identities while honest agents pay only for work they already do.
